raw.author: changmyung1981
raw.text:
🧬💪 What if fatty liver disease and muscle wasting could be improved simultaneously by restoring a shared metabolic signaling pathway—even as body weight increases?

A new study in npj Aging reports that Shenling Baizhu San (SLBZS), a traditional Chinese herbal formulation, improves hepatic steatosis and sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction in rats, accompanied by enhanced AMPKα signaling in both liver and skeletal muscle.

The key finding: Liver–muscle metabolic recovery may occur alongside weight gain, highlighting the importance of body composition rather than body weight alone.

🔬 1. Modeling the MASLD–sarcopenia connection

Researchers used a high-fat, high-sugar (HFHS) diet to induce metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction in male Sprague–Dawley rats.

Experimental design:

• 18 weeks of HFHS diet-induced disease modeling
• 8 weeks of SLBZS treatment
• SLBZS dose: 1.08 g/kg/day
• Final treatment groups: n=6 each
• Total experimental duration: 26 weeks
The HFHS diet produced:
• Hepatic steatosis
• Insulin resistance
• Increased adiposity
• Reduced skeletal muscle mass and strength
• Myosteatosis
• Suppressed AMPKα signaling
Importantly, this was a diet-induced metabolic muscle dysfunction model—not a validated model of human age-related sarcopenia.
⚡ 2. Metabolic dysfunction damages both liver and muscle

After 18 weeks of HFHS feeding, rats exhibited substantial changes in body composition.

ParameterControlHFHSBody weight511.7 g616.3 gGastrocnemius mass3,470 mg3,095 mgSarcopenia index6.6495.012
Despite higher body weight, HFHS-fed rats had lower gastrocnemius mass and reduced muscle strength.
Histological analysis also demonstrated:
• Increased hepatic lipid droplets
• Reduced muscle fiber cross-sectional area
• Increased intramuscular fat deposition
• Muscle fiber disorganization
• Inflammatory infiltration
These findings illustrate how obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction can coexist with skeletal muscle deterioration.
🫀 3. SLBZS improves hepatic steatosis and insulin resistance

Following eight weeks of treatment, SLBZS significantly improved multiple MASLD-associated parameters.

Compared with untreated HFHS-fed rats:

• Hepatic triglycerides ↓
• Hepatic cholesterol ↓
• Liver steatosis area ↓
• NAFLD activity score ↓
• Serum ALT, AST, and GGT ↓
• Triglycerides and LDL cholesterol ↓
• HDL cholesterol ↑
• Fasting glucose and insulin ↓
• HOMA-IR ↓
Histological examination showed substantially fewer hepatic lipid droplets and improved hepatocyte morphology.
These results support an association between SLBZS administration and improved hepatic metabolic homeostasis in this rat model.
💪 4. Muscle mass and strength recover despite weight gain
At week 26, the investigators reported:
ParameterControlHFHSSLBZSBody weight (g)530.8505.8633.8Gastrocnemius mass (mg)3,432.92,872.94,218.7Sarcopenia index6.4675.6826.653
Compared with untreated HFHS-fed rats, SLBZS-treated animals demonstrated:
• Grip strength ↑
• Gastrocnemius wet weight ↑
• Muscle fiber cross-sectional area ↑
• Absolute lean mass ↑
• Fat mass and fat percentage ↓
• Myosteatosis ↓
Notably, muscle-associated improvements occurred despite substantial increases in body weight.
However, food intake also increased during SLBZS treatment, making it difficult to separate direct pharmacological effects from nutritional recovery.
🧬 5. Transcriptomics identifies AMPK as a shared metabolic pathway
Researchers performed RNA sequencing in liver and gastrocnemius muscle.
They identified:
• 518 common differentially expressed genes in liver
• 361 common differentially expressed genes in skeletal muscle
These genes overlapped between disease-associated and treatment-responsive transcriptional changes.
KEGG enrichment analysis highlighted AMPK signaling as a prominent shared pathway.

Gene set enrichment analysis further demonstrated:

• Negative AMPK pathway enrichment under HFHS conditions
• Positive AMPK pathway enrichment following SLBZS treatment

This suggests that AMPK-associated nutrient sensing may contribute to metabolic alterations across both tissues.
However, transcriptomic enrichment alone cannot establish pathway causality.
🔋 6. AMPKα–ACC signaling is restored in liver and muscle
AMPK is a central energy-sensing kinase involved in lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, and cellular nutrient responses.
The HFHS diet was associated with reduced:

• AMPKα phosphorylation
• p-AMPKα/AMPKα ratio
• ACC phosphorylation
• p-ACC/ACC ratio

SLBZS treatment increased these phosphorylation-associated markers in both liver and skeletal muscle.

The proposed metabolic framework is:

AMPKα signaling ↑ → ACC phosphorylation ↑ → Reduced lipogenic activity → Improved lipid homeostasis

Because AMPK-dependent ACC phosphorylation inhibits ACC catalytic activity, increased p-ACC is consistent with reduced malonyl-CoA production and potentially greater fatty acid oxidation.
However, the study did not directly quantify ACC enzymatic activity, malonyl-CoA, or fatty acid oxidation flux.
🔥 7. Lipogenesis decreases while fatty acid oxidation-associated signaling increases
In both liver and skeletal muscle, SLBZS treatment was associated with:
• CPT-1 ↑
• SREBP-1C ↓
• FAS ↓
CPT-1 facilitates mitochondrial import of long-chain fatty acyl groups for β-oxidation.
SREBP-1C regulates transcriptional programs involved in lipogenesis.
FAS contributes to de novo fatty acid synthesis.
The proposed pathway is:

AMPKα activation
↓
ACC phosphorylation ↑
↓
Lipogenic signaling ↓
↓
CPT-1-associated fatty acid oxidation capacity ↑
↓
Hepatic steatosis and myosteatosis ↓

These molecular findings are consistent with improved lipid handling.

Nevertheless, CPT-1 expression does not directly establish increased mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.

⚙️ 8. FOXO1–MAFbx signaling links metabolic dysfunction to muscle loss
The study also examined skeletal muscle protein degradation-associated regulators.
Under HFHS conditions:
• FOXO1 expression ↑
• MAFbx expression ↑
Following SLBZS treatment:
• FOXO1 ↓
• MAFbx ↓
MAFbx, also known as atrogin-1, is an E3 ubiquitin ligase associated with skeletal muscle protein degradation.
FOXO1 can regulate atrophy-associated transcriptional programs.
The authors propose that reduced FOXO1–MAFbx signaling may contribute to improved muscle preservation.
However, FOXO1 phosphorylation, nuclear localization, ubiquitin-proteasome activity, and direct protein turnover were not measured.
Therefore, reduced expression of these markers does not establish that muscle proteolysis was directly inhibited.
🧪 9. Nutrient sensing may connect MASLD and sarcopenia-like dysfunction
The study frames AMPK dysregulation within the hallmarks of aging.
Chronic nutrient excess can contribute to:
• Impaired nutrient sensing
• Insulin resistance
• Lipid accumulation
• Mitochondrial dysfunction
• Chronic inflammation
• Disrupted protein homeostasis
The proposed integrated model is:
HFHS diet → AMPKα signaling ↓
Liver:
ACC phosphorylation ↓ → SREBP-1C/FAS ↑ → Lipogenesis-associated signaling ↑ → Steatosis
Skeletal muscle:
CPT-1 ↓ + FOXO1/MAFbx ↑ → Myosteatosis and atrophy-associated signaling → Muscle dysfunction
SLBZS treatment → AMPKα-associated signaling ↑ → Improved liver and muscle metabolic phenotypes
This framework highlights nutrient sensing as a potential shared regulatory node in metabolic liver–muscle disease.

🎯 10. Therapeutic implications

The findings raise an important possibility:
Treating MASLD complicated by muscle dysfunction may require coordinated improvement in hepatic lipid handling, skeletal muscle metabolism, and protein homeostasis.
AMPKα-associated signaling represents a candidate pathway connecting these processes.
However, SLBZS is a multicomponent herbal formulation, and the study did not identify which individual constituents were responsible for the observed effects.
The results should therefore be interpreted as evidence of a treatment-associated phenotype rather than proof of a specific molecular drug–target interaction.
🚨 11. Critical limitations

Several important issues constrain translation:

• The study used a small number of male rats (n=6 per final group).
• Only one SLBZS dose was tested.
• No metformin or other positive-control treatment was included.
• No AMPK inhibitor, genetic knockout, or knockdown experiment established AMPK dependence.
• Increased food intake may explain part of the observed muscle and body-weight recovery.
• No pair-feeding control was performed.
• Muscle protein synthesis and degradation rates were not directly measured.
• Mitochondrial respiration and fatty acid oxidation flux were not directly quantified.
• Possible interstitial edema could not be completely excluded from muscle mass measurements.
• No clinical trial established efficacy or safety in humans with MASLD and sarcopenia.

Crucially, the results do not demonstrate that SLBZS reverses biological aging or clinically diagnosed sarcopenia.

💡 Key takeaway

MASLD and sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction share metabolic abnormalities involving nutrient sensing, lipid handling, and muscle protein homeostasis.

In this rat study, SLBZS treatment was associated with increased AMPKα signaling, reduced hepatic and skeletal muscle lipid accumulation, and improved muscle mass and strength.
The most important mechanistic question remains unresolved:

Is AMPKα activation necessary for the observed benefits, or does it accompany improved nutritional and metabolic status?

Answering this question will be essential before translating these findings into targeted therapies for MASLD-associated muscle dysfunction.

📄 Yang Y, Song Y, Li J, et al.

Shenling Baizhu San ameliorates MASLD complicated with sarcopenia-like muscle dysfunction in association with AMPKα signaling.
npj Aging (2026). Article in Press.

DOI: https://t.co/CaN5Y604mz

RNA-seq dataset: PRJNA1469358

raw.text:
Very exciting initial preprint illustrating Levels' unparalleled IRB-approved study. The study ran for 3.5 years and included more than 62,000 participants with multi-modal supplemental data alongside CGM.

-Spike duration matters more than peak.

Promising evidence for CGM's role in preventive health, not just diabetes management.

raw.author: DrNikhilMD
raw.text:
🩸 Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM): The Future of Diabetes Care

CGM is one of the most powerful tools in modern diabetology.
It doesn’t just give numbers, it tells the story of a patient’s glucose life in real time.

Unlike HbA1c, which gives a 3-month average, CGM measures interstitial glucose every few minutes, revealing day-to-day fluctuations, nocturnal lows, post-meal spikes, and overall glucose stability.

🔍 Why CGM is Superior to HbA1c in Many Scenarios

HbA1c remains valuable for long-term risk assessment, but it can mislead clinicians in several common conditions.

When CGM is better:
• Anemia, CKD, hemolysis, or recent transfusion – HbA1c is falsely low.
• Iron/B12 deficiency or hypothyroidism – HbA1c is falsely high.
• Pregnancy, steroid therapy, or fluctuating schedules – rapid glucose swings missed by HbA1c.
• Marked variability or hypoglycemia unawareness – same HbA1c, very different risks.

If a patient’s HbA1c looks “perfect” but CGM shows multiple lows or spikes, believe CGM — not the lab.

📊 The 4 Essential CGM Metrics (ADA/EASD Consensus)

✅ Time in Range (TIR) : 70–180 mg/dL → Goal ≥70%
⚠️ Time Below Range (TBR) : <70 mg/dL → Goal <4%
⚡ Time Above Range (TAR) : >180 mg/dL → Goal <25%
📉 Glucose Variability (CV) : Goal <36%

Every 10% rise in TIR ≈ 0.5% reduction in HbA1c — but more importantly, fewer microvascular complications and better quality of life.

🧠 How to Read and Interpret a CGM Report (AGP)

1️⃣ Summary View: Start with TIR, TBR, and CV. this is your control snapshot.
If TBR ≥4%, correct hypoglycemia first before adjusting anything else.

2️⃣ Modal Day Curve: This 14-day overlay highlights patterns.
• Nighttime lows → too much basal insulin
• Early morning highs → dawn phenomenon
• Post-meal peaks → delayed or inadequate bolus

3️⃣ Daily Glucose Traces: Zoom into specific days to identify triggers.
• Weekend highs? → diet or alcohol.
• Day 1 sensor variability? → calibration effect.
• Sporadic drops? → unplanned activity or delayed meals.

💊 CGM-Guided Management Strategies

For Hypoglycemia (TBR ≥4%)
• Stop sulfonylureas if possible.
• Reduce basal insulin by 10–20%.
• If specific lows occur after certain meals, reduce that meal’s bolus by ~10%.
• Persistent daily lows → reduce total daily insulin by 10%.

For Hyperglycemia (TAR ≥25%)
• Rule out missed doses or poor technique.
• Add a GLP-1 receptor agonist (Semaglutide, Tirzepatide) — improves control, reduces weight, and lowers CV risk.
• When adding GLP-1 RA, reduce insulin dose by ~20% if TIR >50% to avoid hypoglycemia.

Always correct technique and behavior before medication:
Check injection site, insulin storage, sensor calibration, and diet timing.

⚖️ Lifestyle & External Influences

• Stress: raises glucose
• Exercise: lowers glucose (watch for delayed lows)
• Alcohol: causes late-night hypoglycemia
• High-dose Vitamin C or Paracetamol: may distort readings in older sensors

🧩 Clinical Pearl

Two patients with the same HbA1c (7%) can have completely different CGM profiles 
One stable, the other with repeated highs and dangerous lows.
Only CGM reveals that difference.

💡 Takeaway

CGM shifts diabetes management from reactive to predictive.
It helps clinicians individualize therapy, prevent emergencies, and empower patients.

HbA1c shows an average.
CGM shows reality.
Always treat the pattern, not the point.

#Diabetes #CGM #Endocrinology #MedTwitter

raw.author: WilliamWallace
raw.text:
Most people assume that bringing down blood sugar after a meal takes a real workout, something like a brisk half hour or a trip to the gym. The research says the amount of movement needed is far smaller than that, and when you move matters even more than how long.

The reason sits in your muscles. When a muscle contracts, it pulls sugar out of the blood without needing insulin to open the door. The protein that carries the sugar in, called GLUT4, rises to the surface of the muscle cell in response to two separate signals, and muscle contraction is one of them. That is why movement lowers blood sugar even in people whose insulin works poorly, and why the effect shows up within minutes instead of after weeks of training.

A 2026 trial tested how little movement it takes. Thirty adults came in on two evenings and drank a standard sugar drink with 75 grams of glucose. On one evening they stayed seated, and on the other they stepped up and down stairs for a single minute at whatever pace felt comfortable. They rated the effort 1.9 out of 10, barely more than sitting. In the hour after the drink, their blood sugar rose about 42 percent less after the minute of stairs than after sitting, and their total sugar exposure across the session was lower too. The researchers chose the evening on purpose, because the same amount of sugar pushes blood sugar higher at night than it does in the morning.

One minute is right at the edge of what works, and it does not work in every situation. The same research group ran the comparison in the morning with bouts of 1, 3 and 10 minutes after the sugar drink. Three and ten minutes lowered blood sugar, while one minute did not come close to making a difference. When they repeated it after a real mixed meal of 650 calories, one minute did help, trimming the blood sugar rise by about 14 points on a standard glucose meter. So a single minute seems to be enough after a normal meal and in the evening, but not reliably after a morning sugar drink. Three minutes worked in every version they tested, which makes three the safer number to aim for.

Timing turned out to matter more than length. A 2023 analysis pooled eight trials with 116 people, about 4 in 10 of whom had type 2 diabetes, and compared exercising before a meal, after a meal, and not at all. Moving after the meal beat moving before it and beat doing nothing. Moving before the meal worked no better than sitting still. The analysis also found that the shorter the gap between finishing the meal and starting to move, the bigger the benefit, so a short walk taken right away does more than a longer one taken an hour later.

The useful change is in the ten minutes after you finish eating. Sitting down is what most of us do by default, and for blood sugar it is one of the weakest choices available. Climb the stairs if you have them or take a walk if you do not, and keep in mind that starting sooner matters more than going longer.

References
Morales et al., Experimental Physiology, 2026
Moore et al., Journal of Exercise Science and Fitness, 2024
Kressler et al., Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases, 2022
Engeroff et al., Sports Medicine, 2023

raw.author: BoboLucyWisdom
raw.text:
如何判断自己或者自己的孩子是否已经胰岛素抵抗了？Dr. Boz提及了四种胰岛素抵抗迹象： 

1） 带小“颈”的皮肤赘生物（腋窝、腹股沟、颈部）。
2） 颈后及褶皱处皮肤呈深色、厚实、丝绒状 → 黑棘皮病。看起来像永久性污垢。
3） 脚趾、脚踝和小腿的毛发逐渐消失。
4） 过早出现白发和加速衰老。  

记住，这些症状都可以通过生酮饮食逆转！
关注我，了解更多生酮自愈路径！
